# workloadctl

> Declarative workload manager for Linux. A TOML file in `/etc/workloads.d/<name>/` becomes a dedicated unprivileged system user, systemd units, storage, secrets, networking and lifecycle, on two substrates: rootless-podman containers and KVM/QEMU virtual machines.

One workload, one unprivileged user (`_wl-<name>`). That uid is the selector everything keys on: egress policy matches it as `meta skuid`, storage is owned by it, the credential broker identifies callers by it, and software inside the workload cannot forge it. Both substrates share one TOML model and one command surface.

workloadctl is stdlib Python 3.14 plus a systemd generator, with no daemon of its own. It runs on ordinary Fedora 43+ and is bootc-ready. It requires moatery, which provides the egress inspector, the credential broker and the DNS responder.

- [Security model](docs/security-model.md)
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): failures, causes and fixes
- [Filtered VM walkthrough](docs/vm-egress-walkthrough.md): one request, from TOML to packet
- [Egress and broker architecture](docs/egress-and-broker-architecture.md)

- [VM virtiofs](docs/vm-virtiofs.md): how guest volumes are shared and confined

- [Design decisions](docs/adr/README.md): ADRs 001 to 009
